fixes.explanation: Synagogue, friend? I love it, you went straight for a holy building! But Paul says this brother is praised by all the churches "…for his work in the gospel." (2 Corinthians 8:18) The gospel, the good news, is the answer. His work is about that, not a building.

Paying his own way, baker? You're thinking like a budget planner, and I respect it. But the text never says who covers the trip. Paul says this brother's earnestness shows "…now even more so by his great confidence in you." (2 Corinthians 8:22) The proof is how much he believes in the Corinthians.

Packing up and leaving home does sound earnest, friend. But that's not where Paul points. He says this brother's earnestness shows "…now even more so by his great confidence in you." (2 Corinthians 8:22) The proof is that he believes in the Corinthians.

Respect for Paul's authority? Friend, Paul isn't asking for applause here. He asks them to "…show these men the proof of your love and the reason for our boasting about you." (2 Corinthians 8:24) Love is on his list, and authority never makes it.

Courage under trial sounds mighty impressive, baker, like a movie trailer. But it's not in this verse. Paul asks the Corinthians to "…show these men the proof of your love and the reason for our boasting about you." (2 Corinthians 8:24) Love is what he names, so love is the answer.

Checking on the teaching sounds like serious business, friend, but nobody's carrying a clipboard for that here. Paul says he's sending the brothers "…in order that our boasting about you in this matter should not prove empty, but that you will be prepared, just as I said." (2 Corinthians 9:3) This trip is about the Corinthians being prepared to give. That's the answer.
